games.title: Hydlide
games.note: First released on Japan's PC-8801 and PC-6001 computers; an early open-world action RPG.

games.title: Legacy of Kain: Soul Reaver
games.note: Directed and written by Amy Hennig before she moved to Naughty Dog.

games.title: Tomb Raider (2013)
games.note: A reboot telling the story of Lara Croft's first expedition, shipwrecked on an island.

games.title: Kill Switch
games.note: Built its combat around snapping into cover and blind-firing.

games.title: Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor
games.note: Its Nemesis System lets orc captains remember you and rise through the ranks.

games.title: Bayonetta
games.note: Directed by Hideki Kamiya, who created Devil May Cry.

games.title: No More Heroes
games.note: Goichi Suda's game, where you save your progress on a toilet.

games.title: Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons
games.note: You steer both brothers at once, one per thumbstick.

games.title: Yooka-Laylee
games.note: Made by former Rare staff after a 2015 Kickstarter.

games.title: A Hat in Time
games.note: Kickstarted in 2013 to revive the 3D collect-a-thon platformer.

games.title: Astro's Playroom
games.note: Came preinstalled on every PlayStation 5 to show off the DualSense controller.

games.title: Astro Bot
games.note: Won Game of the Year at The Game Awards 2024. Directed by Nicolas Doucet.

games.title: Beyond Good & Evil
games.note: Created by Michel Ancel, who also made Rayman.

games.title: Tunic
games.note: Hides its rules in an in-game instruction manual you collect page by page.

games.title: Death's Door
games.note: Acid Nerve is essentially two people, David Fenn and Mark Foster.

games.title: Hyper Light Drifter
games.note: Alx Preston has said his own heart condition shaped the game's themes.

games.title: Outer Wilds
games.note: Began as Alex Beachum's master's thesis project at USC.

games.title: Kena: Bridge of Spirits
games.note: Ember Lab began as an animation studio and made a Majora's Mask fan film in 2016.

links.took: The idea: Miyamoto conceived a 3D Mario while making Star Fox on the Super FX chip.
links.added: Moved it to the Nintendo 64, using the analog stick for free 3D movement.
links.extra: Miyamoto reworked the idea for the N64 because of its controller, not its power.

links.took: Its engine: Ocarina first ran on Super Mario 64's engine, later heavily modified.
links.added: Z-targeting lock-on and context-sensitive buttons for 3D sword combat.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

links.extra: The two were developed at the same time at Nintendo EAD.

links.took: Open 3D worlds full of collectibles; Gregg Mayles set Super Mario 64 as the target to beat.
links.added: A bear-and-bird duo, a witch's lair as the hub and lots of humor.
links.extra: Rare scrapped much of its earlier project, Dream, after seeing Super Mario 64.

links.took: Rare's team: Project Dream, which became Banjo-Kazooie, began right after Donkey Kong Country 2.
links.added: Moved from 2D sidescrolling to full 3D on the Nintendo 64.
links.extra: Pirate enemies and tropical areas in Banjo-Kazooie trace back to Dream.

links.took: Controls and environmental design, cited as influences by Michael John, who worked on Spyro.
links.added: Gliding, charging and flaming, with gem-filled worlds to roam.

links.took: Direct 3D character movement; Tim Schafer called it the biggest single influence.
links.added: Levels set inside people's minds, each with its own art and logic.

links.took: The concept: Tim Schafer first had the idea while making Full Throttle.
links.added: Built it as Double Fine's first game, a psychic summer-camp platformer.

links.took: Named by Gabe Newell as an inspiration; the source doesn't say which part.
links.added: A science-fiction shooter told without cutscenes, from the player's own eyes.

links.took: Its hub world, on which director Ashraf Ismail based Black Flag's open world.
links.added: A sailing Caribbean of islands, forts and sea battles.

links.took: 3D environments built for exploration, which Square Enix said inspired the series.
links.added: Disney worlds, Final Fantasy characters and real-time action-RPG combat.

links.took: A big 3D world, a goal inspired by the success of games like Super Mario 64.
links.added: One seamless world with no loading screens between areas.

src.t: Wikipedia: Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy

links.took: Platforming elements, which Naughty Dog paired with Zelda-style epic storytelling.
links.added: A seamless world and a sidekick who never stops talking.

src.t: Wikipedia: Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy

links.took: Naughty Dog's platforming, and a goal set by the limits of Crash's separate levels.
links.added: Free roaming in place of corridors, streamed without loading screens.

src.t: Wikipedia: Jak and Daxter: The Precursor Legacy

links.took: Technology: Insomniac shared tech with Naughty Dog, which built some key renderers.
links.added: Collectible gadget weapons and a sci-fi galaxy of planets.
links.extra: Ted Price said: 'Naughty Dog's generosity gave us a huge leg up.'

links.took: Insomniac's 3D platforming know-how from its Spyro games.
links.added: A gun-heavy action platformer with upgradable weapons and humor.

links.took: A mascot with attitude; the project's joke codename was 'Sonic's Ass Game'.
links.added: Running into the screen in 3D, with boulder chases toward the camera.

src.t: Rolling Stone, Crash Bandicoot oral history, 2016
Wikipedia: Sonic the Hedgehog (1991 video game)

links.took: A character platformer in DKC's vein, plus its jungle setting, per Andy Gavin.
links.added: Full 3D depth on PlayStation, with crates to smash and Wumpa fruit.

src.t: Rolling Stone, Crash Bandicoot oral history, 2016

links.took: Naughty Dog's team, including Amy Hennig, who worked on the Jak games.
links.added: A realistic treasure hunter, cover shooting and film-like set pieces.

links.took: Amy Hennig, who directed Soul Reaver before leading Uncharted.
links.added: A pulp adventure with Nathan Drake, a claimed descendant of Sir Francis Drake.

links.took: Cover-based third-person shooting, named by the developers alongside Kill Switch.
links.added: Mixed cover fights with climbing, puzzles and a treasure-hunt story.

links.took: Snapping into cover and blind-firing, named by Naughty Dog as an influence.
links.added: Jungles, ruins and wisecracking banter around the gunfights.

links.took: Over-the-shoulder action, cited by the developers as an influence.
links.added: Treasure hunting, climbing and a lighter, pulpy tone.

links.took: Platforming and shooting through ancient ruins, earning the nickname 'Dude Raider'.
links.added: Cover-based gunfights instead of auto-aim, plus cinematic storytelling.
links.extra: Naughty Dog contrasted its cover-based play with Tomb Raider's auto-aiming.

links.took: Character building through interaction; Neil Druckmann credits Ico's gameplay as a key inspiration.
links.added: A man and a girl crossing a ruined America, with stealth and crafting.
links.extra: Druckmann has called Ico his favorite game of all time.

links.took: Naughty Dog's team; an idea from Uncharted 2's development led to The Last of Us.
links.added: Survival tension, scarce supplies and a quieter, grimmer story.

links.took: A believable castle where you always know where you are, per director Patrice Desilets.
links.added: Wall-running acrobatics and the Dagger of Time to rewind mistakes.

src.t: Wikipedia: Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time

links.extra: Jordan Mechner also cited Ico as influencing the game's visuals.

links.took: Its engine: Sands of Time used an updated Jade engine, built for Beyond Good & Evil.
links.added: Fluid acrobatics, time rewind and a story narrated by the Prince.

src.t: Wikipedia: Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time

links.extra: Both came out in November 2003.

links.took: The rewind feature, which Wikipedia says this earlier Ubisoft Montreal game inspired.
links.added: Made rewinding a core power, fed by sand from the Dagger of Time.

src.t: Wikipedia: Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time

links.took: Its sequel plans: work began as 'Prince of Persia: Assassin' under Patrice Desilets.
links.added: Dropped the prince for an assassin in open cities you climb freely.

src.t: Wikipedia: Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time

links.took: Open-world freedom, a concept Wikipedia says came from the success of Grand Theft Auto.
links.added: Historical cities, crowd blending and assassination targets.

links.took: Its creator, Michel Ancel, and Ubisoft Montpellier's team.
links.added: A photojournalist exposing a conspiracy, with hovercraft travel and wildlife photography.

links.took: The UbiArt Framework look, four-player co-op and Rayman's cast.
links.added: Music levels synced to songs and Murfy touch-screen stages.

links.took: Visual appearance; Eiji Aonuma cited Ico as influencing how his game looked.
links.added: A darker Hyrule, a wolf transformation and Midna as companion.

links.took: Visual appearance; Hideo Kojima cited Ico as influencing the look of his game.
links.added: Jungle survival, camouflage and a Cold War spy story.

links.took: Hidetaka Miyazaki cites Ico as a key reason he got into game development.
links.added: Punishing online action-RPG combat and a world told in fragments.
links.extra: The influence is on Miyazaki's career; Demon's Souls was the first Souls game he directed.

links.took: Wordless emotion and companionship; Jenova Chen cites Ico as one of his biggest influences.
links.added: Anonymous online strangers who travel together without words.

links.took: Ico's save method, which Goichi Suda says inspired how you save.
links.added: Saving on a toilet instead of a stone bench.

links.took: Puzzle-solving between fights; Wikipedia describes God of War as mixing Devil May Cry's action with Ico's puzzles.
links.added: Brutal Greek-myth combat, quick-time finishers and huge set pieces.

src.t: Wikipedia: God of War (2005 video game)

links.took: A wordless journey built on companionship, listed by Wikipedia among Ico-inspired games.
links.added: Controlling two brothers at once, one per thumbstick.

links.took: Listed by Wikipedia among games inspired by Ico; the source doesn't say which part.
links.added: Desert treks, a sinking cruise ship and Drake's past with Sully.

links.took: Ruins, a lonely island and wordless puzzle-solving, listed among Ico-inspired games.
links.added: Bright, painterly colors and a story about loss.

links.took: Fumito Ueda's team and the bond between a boy and his companion.
links.added: A giant feathered beast, Trico, who acts on its own will.

links.took: Named by Fumito Ueda among Ico's influences, alongside Lemmings and Flashback.
links.added: Animation-led 3D movement in a quiet castle instead of a fighting ring.

links.took: Traps and chasms; Toby Gard called Tomb Raider a transition between Prince of Persia and Indiana Jones.
links.added: Full 3D tombs, a female archaeologist hero and dual pistols.

src.t: Toby Gard, PLAY interview, 1996, via core-design.com

links.took: Exploring connected 3D spaces; Toby Gard listed it among the game's sources in 1996.
links.added: Third-person climbing, jumping and swimming through tombs.

src.t: Toby Gard, PLAY interview, 1996, via core-design.com

links.took: Named by Toby Gard among the game and film sources behind Tomb Raider.
links.added: A polygon heroine exploring 3D tombs, seen from behind.

src.t: Toby Gard, PLAY interview, 1996, via core-design.com

links.took: Core Design's earlier Indiana Jones-style, trap-filled adventure platformer.
links.added: Full 3D exploration and a new hero, Lara Croft.
links.extra: Studio lineage only; Toby Gard did not design Rick Dangerous.

links.took: Lara Croft, tombs and climbing.
links.added: A rebooted origin story, a darker tone and survival crafting.

links.took: Combat that borrows multiple elements from Naughty Dog's Uncharted series.
links.added: Bow hunting, salvage upgrades and a semi-open island.

links.took: The rebooted Lara, survival crafting and hub areas.
links.added: Bigger optional tombs, Siberian wilds and a story about immortality.

src.t: Wikipedia: Rise of the Tomb Raider

links.took: 3D action-adventure design; Amy Hennig noted Ocarina of Time's influence on Soul Reaver.
links.added: Shifting between material and spectral planes, and devouring souls.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

links.took: A model for 3D action; Hidetaka Miyazaki called Zelda 'a sort of textbook' for it.
links.added: An interlocking world, punishing combat and messages from other players.

src.t: Wikipedia: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

links.extra: Miyazaki spoke of the Zelda series; Wikipedia's Ocarina of Time article cites it in its legacy section.

links.took: Items that open new areas; Sefton Hill called Zelda and Metroid big influences.
links.added: Freeflow combat, predator stealth and detective vision.

links.took: An interconnected island you reopen with new gadgets, a Metroid-style structure.
links.added: Batman's gadgets, his villains and Riddler secrets in place of power-ups.

links.took: Rhythmic freeflow combat and stealth, which Wikipedia says largely shaped its fighting.
links.added: The Nemesis System: orc captains who remember you and rise through ranks.

links.took: Climbing, stealth kills and open-world traversal, called its inspirations by reviewers.
links.added: Wraith powers to brand and control enemy orcs.

links.took: Counter-based melee and gadget combat, which reviewers compared to the Arkham series.
links.added: Web-swinging across Manhattan and aerial combat.
links.extra: USGamer called the Arkham comparisons unfair, pointing to Spider-Man's range of gadgets.

links.took: A bug where enemies could be kept in the air by slashing, found by Hideki Kamiya.
links.added: Turned juggling into a combo system with guns and swords, plus style ranks.

links.took: Capcom's Resident Evil team: Devil May Cry began as the earliest version of Resident Evil 4.
links.added: Gothic demon-hunting action with a cocky hero, Dante.
links.extra: Director Hideki Kamiya had directed Resident Evil 2.

links.took: Acrobatic, stylish sword action, which Eurogamer called a vital influence.
links.added: 3D combo combat mixing swords and guns, graded by a style meter.

src.t: Eurogamer, via Wikipedia: Devil May Cry

links.took: Stylish combo combat; Hideki Kamiya says Bayonetta evolved from Devil May Cry.
links.added: Witch Time slowdown after dodging and over-the-top finishing moves.

links.took: Action with mythology; David Jaffe played Onimusha and said 'let's do that with Greek mythology'.
links.added: Kratos's chained blades, quick-time kills and huge Greek-myth set pieces.

src.t: Wikipedia: God of War (2005 video game)

links.took: Combo-based action, which Wikipedia describes God of War as merging with Ico's puzzles.
links.added: Greek mythology, brutal finishers and a cinematic fixed camera.

src.t: Wikipedia: God of War (2005 video game)

links.took: Acrobatic combat and set pieces, which Eurogamer considered a vital influence.
links.added: The Blades of Chaos and Greek gods as allies and enemies.

src.t: Eurogamer, via Wikipedia: God of War (2005)

links.took: Combo-driven action combat, compared by critics to God of War.
links.added: Zelda-style dungeons and tools in a post-apocalyptic world.

links.took: Fast, stylish melee combat, one of three series critics used to describe it.
links.added: A horseman of the apocalypse, big puzzle dungeons and comic-book art by Joe Madureira.

links.took: Hidden secrets and exploration; Tokihiro Naito was inspired especially by Druaga.
links.added: An open field to roam, real-time combat and health that refills when you rest.

links.took: Japanese computer role-playing, which Naito named as an inspiration.
links.added: Real-time action combat instead of turn-based battles.
links.extra: Naito said he was unaware of Western RPGs like Ultima and Wizardry at the time.

links.took: Open-world design; Wikipedia says Hideo Kojima drew on Hydlide for The Phantom Pain.
links.added: Stealth across open regions of Afghanistan and Africa, with a base to grow.

links.took: Hub-based 3D platforming, named by designer Jonas Kaerlev as a huge inspiration.
links.added: A girl with magic hats, Time Pieces and chapters like a train murder mystery.

links.took: The N64 collect-a-thon style, which Kaerlev set out to revive.
links.added: Hats that grant powers, and badges to customize moves.

links.took: Compact sandbox levels, named by Kaerlev as a huge inspiration.
links.added: A cast of oddballs like the Snatcher, and bosses with personality.

links.took: Imaginative themed worlds and humor, named by Kaerlev as a huge inspiration.
links.added: Short chapters that switch genre, from mystery to horror to film studio.

links.took: Rare's N64 3D platforming, which Kaerlev named among the game's roots.
links.added: A cute art style with sudden dark jokes.

links.took: Former Rare staff and Banjo-Kazooie's style, with a pair of heroes.
links.added: A crowdfunded return starring a chameleon and a bat.

links.took: Producers Yoshiaki Koizumi and Koichi Hayashida, the same pair behind 3D World.
links.added: Cappy, a hat that lets Mario possess enemies and objects.
links.extra: Directed by Kenta Motokura.

links.took: Sandbox play; Miyamoto said the series would go back to its roots, to Sunshine.
links.added: Kingdoms packed with hundreds of Power Moons to find.

links.took: Exploration-based level design, which Odyssey's kingdoms return to.
links.added: Possession via Cappy and travel between themed kingdoms in a hat-shaped ship.

links.took: Nintendo EPD's Odyssey team, which began Bananza after finishing Odyssey.
links.added: Destructible voxel worlds and Donkey Kong's animal Bananza transformations.
links.extra: Odyssey director Kenta Motokura produced Bananza.

links.took: Breaking blocks; producer Kenta Motokura was inspired by Super Mario Bros.' second level.
links.added: Punching and digging through entire worlds, not just bricks.

links.took: Astro and his move set from the VR platformer.
links.added: A flat-screen showcase for the DualSense controller, preinstalled on PS5.

links.took: Astro's move set and the PlayStation cameos, which the team chose to double down on.
links.added: A full-length adventure across many planets, rescuing hundreds of cameo bots.
links.extra: Critics compared it favorably to Nintendo's Super Mario games.

links.took: Varied, themed 3D platforming levels, the genre Super Mario 64 popularized.
links.added: DualSense-driven gadgets and hundreds of PlayStation cameo bots to rescue.
links.extra: No developer statement names Mario; critics compared Astro Bot favorably to the Super Mario series.

links.took: A world on a repeating time loop; Alex Beachum cited Majora's Mask in his original pitch.
links.added: A whole solar system that resets every 22 minutes, explored through knowledge alone.

src.t: LevelUp, on Outer Wilds' Zelda inspirations
Alex Beachum, Road to the IGF, Gamasutra

links.extra: Beachum says the loop serves large dynamic systems, unlike Majora's Mask's play with cause and effect.

links.took: Free exploration; the thesis-era structure came from Wind Waker's photography sidequest.
links.added: A tiny spaceship and a translator for an extinct alien race's writing.
links.extra: Beachum told Edge that Outer Wilds has more in common with The Wind Waker than Majora's Mask.

links.took: The first Zelda's promise of a big world to explore, Andrew Shouldice's touchstone.
links.added: An in-game manual in a made-up language that hides the rules.
links.extra: Shouldice: 'Of all the Zelda games, the one I find myself thinking of most is the very first one.'

links.took: Interconnected world design; Shouldice had played the Souls games and admired their worlds.
links.added: A small fox hero and shortcuts looping through a cute isometric world.

links.took: Combat feel; Shouldice says Bloodborne had the most direct kinaesthetic influence.
links.added: Stamina-based dodging and parrying seen from an isometric camera.

links.took: Isometric visuals; Shouldice named Monument Valley among isometric games he loves.
links.added: An explorable isometric world with combat and hidden secrets.

links.took: The fast, arcade-like combat flow of A Link to the Past, per David Fenn.
links.added: A crow reaper collecting souls, with tough bosses and a lighthearted tone.

src.t: David Fenn and Mark Foster, NME

links.extra: Fenn sums it up as 'Zelda but with intense combat'.

links.took: World design, which David Fenn drew from A Link Between Worlds.
links.added: Interlocking areas with shortcuts and hidden upgrades.

src.t: David Fenn and Mark Foster, NME

links.took: Interconnected, looping levels with shortcuts, which Mark Foster drew from FromSoftware.
links.added: Cute characters set against themes of death.

src.t: David Fenn and Mark Foster, NME

links.extra: Fenn said he doesn't think it has much in common with Dark Souls beyond shortcuts and looping maps.

links.took: Top-down sword exploration; the Kickstarter said it plays like A Link to the Past and Diablo.
links.added: Dash-heavy combat, wordless storytelling and neon pixel art.

links.took: Fast top-down action, the other half of the Kickstarter pitch.
links.added: Sword and gun combat without loot, set in a ruined, beautiful world.

links.took: Dungeons, puzzles and exploration; Mike Grier named the Zelda games as inspirations.
links.added: Film-quality animation and the Rot, tiny spirits who help in fights and puzzles.

src.t: Mike Grier, Unreal Engine developer interview

links.took: A spirit-guide heroine healing a corrupted land, from a game Mike Grier named.
links.added: Bow and staff combat with Rot companions.

src.t: Mike Grier, Unreal Engine developer interview

updates.why: Tomb Raider (1996) was made by Core Design in Derby, England; Crystal Dynamics took over the series later. Toby Gard designed Lara Croft at Core.
